page: Microsoft Azure F8-2amds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Famdsv7 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture, featuring 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 48 KB L1D cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. This instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 32.0 GB per core. It includes a 945 GB local storage disk and is Premium Storage capable, but does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU, geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scores all placing in the top tier (top 10%). However, multi-core and multi-threaded performance scales down, with stress-ng multi-core, geekbench multi-core, and passmark memory scores falling into the average category. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, clang software compilation, and ray tracing benchmarks are relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is moderate, measuring 402.64 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 52.38 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and strong single-core execution, this server is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallelization. Appropriate use cases include database operations, caching layers like Redis (which achieves 6.72 million operations per second), and text processing. It is less optimal for highly parallelized tasks, software compilation, or medium-to-large language model inference, where prompt processing speeds drop significantly.
